articles.title: Stuttgart
articles.description: A city walk through Stuttgart's layered urban landscape, where modern architecture, surviving fragments, hills, and afternoon light meet.
articles.author: Ugur Kostak
articles.content: This Stuttgart set follows the city from Schlossplatz outward, looking for the quiet tension between post-war surfaces and older architectural traces. The longer metadata mirrors the page's focus on late-afternoon light, minimal equipment, and the small juxtapositions that make the city visually layered.

articles.title: Strasbourg
articles.description: A winter walk through Strasbourg's canals, half-timbered houses, sandstone details, and French-German street rhythm.
articles.author: Ugur Kostak
articles.content: The Strasbourg gallery leans into the city's mixed visual language: gothic sandstone, quiet canals, half-timbered houses, and narrow lanes softened by winter light. The expanded summary gives the listing enough context to feel like a photographic note rather than only a location label.

articles.title: Athens
articles.description: A street-level Athens series that looks beyond monuments toward cafes, graffiti, neighborhoods, cats, and Mediterranean winter light.
articles.author: Ugur Kostak
articles.content: Athens is summarized here as a lived city rather than a postcard of ruins. The listing now points toward the page's quieter details: Exarcheia mornings, Plaka shadows, Monastiraki stalls, warm stone, and the everyday texture below the Acropolis skyline.

articles.title: Istanbul
articles.description: A Bosphorus-facing Istanbul series about ferries, bridges, minarets, rooftops, and the city's constant movement between continents.
articles.author: Ugur Kostak
articles.content: The Istanbul metadata now reflects the page's sense of a city in motion: fishermen on Galata Bridge, commuters, mosques catching afternoon light, and the Bosphorus tying the frames together. It keeps the emphasis on return visits, shifting seasons, and small observations rather than a checklist of landmarks.
